Resolves #19225

A dragged vessel now follows the pointer with its content, not its frame. The drag follow measures its grab offset inside the dragged element and then placed the popup's frame at pointer minus offset, so on a real window the content sat one title bar (67 px on macOS Chrome) below the pointer. Under viewport emulation a popup carries no chrome, which is why the tour never showed it and why the film's capture mode never converted: the two inner rects overlapped a fifth on the y axis against the 0.55 threshold. `Main#windowMoveTo` learns a `contentOrigin` request that places the frame one chrome height above the named point (`outerWidth − innerWidth`, `outerHeight − innerHeight`, read from the same-origin popup at move time); the follow in `DragDrop` asks for it. The park and resume choreography keeps its frame semantics untouched: the park's cover geometry is a frame placement by design, and the resume's grab-offset rebase is frame-based on both sides of its subtraction, so it stays chrome-neutral.

Evidence: L3 achieved (one headed capture-mode run of the film on the film-stage display at this head: the compose beat converts and the whole film completes) → L3 required (AC-2). Residual: none.

## Deltas from ticket
The ticket's fix step named the follow subtracting the chrome "on every follow frame" and correcting the birth position on the first framed frame. The subtraction lives in `Main#windowMoveTo` behind `contentOrigin`, where the popup's metrics are readable, and the follow's first frame after birth is that correction: the vessel is born at the proxy's screen point as a frame and lands one chrome height higher on the first pointer move (16–33 ms into the drag in the film).

## Comments

### `@neo-fable` commented on 2026-09-25T20:05:06Z

**Closed unmerged by the author — the premise was wrong.** The dragged vessel's frame riding the logical drag origin is the design, not a defect: ADR 0029 §2.8.6 has the pointer-follow resume "at the live logical drag origin after restoring the exact pre-conversion outer extent", and the reason the operator gave is the one that matters — with the pointer at the window's corner the dragged window sits below and right of it, so the drop targets around the pointer stay uncovered; anchoring the content would put the title bar over them. I built on a geometry inference and a green run instead of the design record's sentence.

What the receipts do show survives in #19225, restated: with real window chrome the conversion metric (inner rects, min-axis, 0.55) admits equal-size windows only while the pointer is within roughly the top 26 px of the target's content, against about 108 px under viewport emulation, which is why the film's capture mode never converts at the driver's inner-centre aim and why the tour never showed it. Whether that is answered on the metric's plane (frame rects), its thresholds, or the driver's aim is a §2.8 design call, and the ticket names the fork.

Nothing from this branch should land; the branch is deleted with this close.

🪢 Mnemosyne (Claude Fable 5.1 · Claude Code)
